properties.title: NRC Report: Mineral Oil in Storm Drain/Private Pond near Wooster, OH
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 954391 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: AEP OHIO POWER COMPANY
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 954391
Incident Time: 2010-09-17 16:44:00
Nearest City: Wooster, OH
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: MINERAL OIL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: AEP OHIO POWER COMPANY
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 30 gallons
TWO 37.5KVA POLE-MOUNTED TRANSFORMERS WERE DAMAGED DURING A TORNADO AT THE SITE. APPROXIMATELY 30 GALLONS OF NON-PCB MINERAL OIL WERE RELEASED WHEN THE POLE THE TRANSFORMERS WERE MOUNTED TO, WAS SHEARED OFF DURING A TORNADO. WHEN THE SITE WAS FIRST DISCOVERED, THE EMPLOYEES DID NOT SEE A STORM DRAIN IN THE VICINITY WHERE THE TRANSFORMERS FELL. IT WAS ONLY AFTER OUR SPILL CLEANUP CONTRACTOR (SUNPRO) ARRIVED AT THE SITE TO BEGIN THE CLEANUP OF THE RELEASED MATERIAL, THAT THE STORM DRAIN WAS DISCOVERED, AND A SHEEN OBSERVED ON A SMALL POND LOCATED DOWN GRADIENT FROM THE SPILL SITE. SUNPRO IS ONSITE NOW, AND IS DEPLOYING BOOMS AND OTHER MATERIALS TO RECOVER THE RELEASED OIL.

Report Details

Incident Time: 2012-11-12 17:20:00
Nearest City: New York, NY
Location: NATIONAL GRID’S NYC OPERATING AREA
Incident Type: PIPELINE
Material:
Medium Affected: OTHER
Suspected Responsible Party:
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 40.721141, -74.009089 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Report Description
POST-TROPICAL STORM “SANDY” HIT NATIONAL GRID’S NYC OPERATING AREA ON OCT. 29TH, WITH EFFECTS STRONGLY FELT THROUGH OCT. 31ST. STORM SURGE, AN ASTRONOMICAL HIGH TIDE, RAIN AND STRONG WINDS CAUSED EXTENSIVE FLOODING AND DAMAGE TO CUSTOMER PREMISES. SEVERAL SECTIONS OF OUR LOW PRESSURE DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM EXPERIENCED WATER INTRUSION. A NUMBER OF MAINS AND SERVICES ADJACENT TO DESTROYED OR BADLY DAMAGED BUILDINGS WERE CUT OFF FOR SAFETY. SOME SECTIONS OF THE DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM FEEDING DEVASTATED AREAS WERE SHUT DOWN AS WELL, PENDING REPAIR AND REPLACEMENT OPERATIONS. ON NOV. 7TH, A NOR’EASTER STORM HIT THE SAME AREAS WITH HIGH WINDS AND SEVERAL INCHES OF HEAVY SNOW. INSPECTIONS AND ANY NEEDED REPAIRS TO OUR FACILITIES ARE PROGRESSING WELL. INSPECTION OF CUSTOMERS’ METER SETS, APPLIANCES AND ACCESSIBLE INSIDE PIPING IS NEARING COMPLETION. NATIONAL GRID IS UTILIZING ESTABLISHED PROCEDURES TO ISOLATE AND TAG COMPROMISED EQUIPMENT AS WE FIND IT. NUMEROUS PREMISES WILL REQUIRE PROFESSIONAL PLUMBING AND ELECTRICAL INSPECTION, AND THEN REPAIR OR REPLACEMENT OF WIRING, HEATING AND OTHER GAS EQUIPMENT THAT WAS INUNDATED BY SEAWATER. FURTHER DETAILS WILL BE SUPPLIED IN A WRITTEN REPORT.
